title: THE FIRST SLAM DUNK
summary: A 124-minute theatrical film (2022-12-03) that Takehiko Inoue wrote and directed himself — the official STAFF page reads 原作・脚本・監督 井上雄彦 — and whose game half animates the one thing the 1993-96 TV series never reached: Shohoku vs Sannoh Kogyo, the Inter-High second-round match that closes the manga. MangaUpdates' segment FOR THIS ENTRY pins it 'Vol 25, Chap 223 (The First Slam Dunk)' → 'Vol 31, Chap 276 (The First Slam Dunk) Abridged and different with an original epilogue', and the content matches on both ends: the film's first on-court beat is Miyagi's alley-oop ambush to Sakuragi, which is ch 223 「奇襲」 (en-WP's chapter list: 'Surprise Attack'; the fandom's vol 25 summary: 'The match finally begins, and Miyagi and Sakuragi start by making an ambush. Off an alley-oop from Miyagi, Sakuragi makes the first two points'), and its last is Sakuragi's buzzer-beater and the silent hand-slap in ch 276 「湘北高校バスケットボール部」, the manga's final chapter. Interleaved with the game, in four blocks, is a wholly ORIGINAL Ryota Miyagi backstory — Okinawa, his drowned brother Sota, his mother Kaoru and sister Anna, his first year at Shohoku, the moped crash, the return to the island — plus an original ending (Ryota and Kaoru on the beach; Ryota and Sawakita meeting in America years later, which the fandom's Sawakita page flags in as many words: 'although these scenes didn't happen in the manga'); ja-WP records that the top credit is Ryota, not Sakuragi, and en-WP states the film 'adapts the final match depicted in the manga and features original flashbacks and a new epilogue, all centered on Ryota'. That original share is substantial and story-carrying — it is the film's spine, not a garnish — so under T28 the standing is MIXED, not canon-with-divergence; the source share is likewise substantial (the whole 40-minute game, abridged: whole manga beats such as the Sakuragi/Mikio Kawata duel are cut and the Sannoh players' own backstories are condensed). Two findings the sitting should have: the film RETELLS NOTHING the TV run adapted — the run's last adapted chapter is 197 (vol 22 「バッシュ (brand-new)」, ep 96 「バスケットシューズII」, 1996-02-10) and eps 97-101 are anime-original as stored — so chapters 198-222 (the entire Toyotama match, ch 215 「ヤマオー」, and the Sannoh build-up) have never been animated by ANY Slam Dunk anime; and the film's Ryota material is only 'partially the underlying basis'-derived from Inoue's uncollected 1998 one-shot 「ピアス」 (WSJ 1998 #9, 39 pp), an unnumbered side story with no mainline chapter number — a fact, never a number.

chapters_adapted.note: vols 25-31 — the Shohoku vs Sannoh Kogyo match from the tip-off ambush (ch 223 「奇襲」) to the buzzer-beater and hand-slap of the manga's last chapter (276 「湘北高校バスケットボール部」), told ABRIDGED. MangaUpdates' own segment for this film gives exactly this span ('Vol 25, Chap 223' → 'Vol 31, Chap 276 … Abridged and different with an original epilogue'); en-WP: 'the film adapts the final match depicted in the manga'. NOT adapted: the pre-game chapters 216-222 (Shohoku watching last year's final on video, the Sannoh scouting of Shohoku, the day before, the pre-match warm-up) — no source credits them to the film, and the film opens on an original hand-drawn walk-out sequence instead. Ch 276 is PARTIAL: the film stops at the game's end; 276's own post-game epilogue (the third-round defeat to Aiwa, Haruko's letter, Rukawa at the All-Japan camp, Sakuragi in rehabilitation) is replaced by the film's original epilogue. Within the span the abridgement is real — e.g. the Sakuragi vs Mikio Kawata (河田美紀男) duel is cut whole, and the Sannoh players' backstory chapters are condensed — but those are faithfulness-clause cuts of the source's own events, not what makes this row mixed.

position.why: THE FILM CONTINUES THE RUN; IT RETELLS NOTHING OF IT. The TV series' last adapted chapter is 197 (vol 22 「バッシュ (brand-new)」): MangaUpdates' TV segment ends 'Vol 22, Chap 197 (TV)'; ja-WP's テレビアニメ section says 「インターハイに出場決定して試合会場に出発するところまでがアニメ化された」 and names the closing Shoyo/Ryonan combined-team block as anime-original; ep 96 is titled 「バスケットシューズII」 (1996-02-10) and the fandom's synopsis for it is ch 197's story (Sakuragi's shoes tear and he goes back to the man who gave him his first pair). Eps 97-101 — Uozumi's return and the four-part practice game against a Shoyo/Ryonan combined team — adapt nothing and are typed filler as stored; ep 101 closes on the team boarding the Shinkansen for the Inter-High. The film's material starts 26 chapters later, at ch 223, so 101.5 (immediately after the last episode) is correct: there is no overlap to avoid and no re-watch to warn about. THE HONEST CAVEAT BELONGS ON THE ROW: chs 198-222 — the whole Toyotama match (198-214), ch 215 「ヤマオー」 and the Sannoh build-up (216-222) — are animated NOWHERE (the four 1994-95 Toei films are original stories set around the Kanagawa qualifiers, per ja-WP's 劇場アニメ list), so a viewer moving from ep 101 to this film skips 25 chapters that exist only in print. (96.5 would be equivalent in pure source terms, since eps 97-101 adapt nothing, but the film is a continuation released after the whole run and the original block itself sets up the Inter-High departure — after 101 is the right place.)

flags_for_sean: STANDING = MIXED, AND HERE IS THE SIZING. Source share: the entire Sannoh game, chs 223-276, which is the film's backbone and the bulk of its 124 minutes (ja-WP's ストーリー splits it 試合前半 / 試合後半 with the flashbacks cut in between). Original share: four flashback blocks plus the epilogue, all Ryota's — Okinawa and his brother Sota, the father's death, Sota's drowning, the move to Kanagawa, the junior-high 1-on-1 with a boy who turns out to be Mitsui, the gang fight, the moped crash, the flight back to Okinawa and the discovery of Sota's shoes and the Sannoh magazine, the birthday cake, the letter to his mother — none of which is in the 276-chapter manga, and all of which carries the film's plot (ja-WP: 「トップクレジットは原作の主人公の桜木花道ではなく、本作の主人公である宮城リョータになっている」; en-WP: 'original flashbacks and a new epilogue, all centered on Ryota'). That clears T28's materiality bar on both sides: mixed, not canon + divergence, and not filler.

TV-RUN FRONTIER SETTLED AS A BY-PRODUCT (the context prints 'max adapted by the run ?'). The run's last adapted chapter is 197 (vol 22 「バッシュ (brand-new)」) at ep 96 「バスケットシューズII」 (1996-02-10) — MangaUpdates 'Vol 22, Chap 197 (TV)'; ja-WP 「インターハイに出場決定して試合会場に出発するところまでがアニメ化された」; the fandom's ep-96 synopsis is ch 197's story; and the title chain holds around it (ep 88 「バスケットの国アメリカ」 ≈ ch 189 「バスケットの国」, ep 91 「全国が危ない!」 = ch 193 「全国が危ない」, ep 93 「2万本への挑戦」 = the 20,000-shot training of chs 194-196). Eps 94, 95 and 97-101 are anime-original, exactly as stored. This is an episode-row fact outside a related-work verdict's remit — delivered as a note, no anchors proposed here.

NEVER-ANIMATED GAP: 198-222. The Toyotama match (198-214), ch 215 「ヤマオー」 and the Sannoh build-up (216-222) are adapted by nothing in the franchise — not the TV run (which stops at 197), not this film (which starts at 223), and not the four 1994-95 Toei films, whose ja-WP entries describe them as original practice-match stories set around the Kanagawa qualifiers (the second one arranges ch 79's digest of the Tsukubu game). Worth surfacing on the row: 25 chapters of the source exist only in print between ep 101 and this film.

AUTHOR'S HAND ≠ ADOPTION (T26), SO `adopted` IS NULL. The film is 原作・脚本・監督 井上雄彦 (official STAFF page, slamdunk-movie.jp/about/staff/), which is as strong an author credit as exists — but adoption means the source line taking the material in, and the manga ended in 1996 and has not been extended; none of Sota, Kaoru or the American epilogue has been written into a numbered chapter. If Sean wants Inoue's authorship recorded it belongs as a note on the row, never as a standing, and it does not turn the flashbacks into instrument content.

「ピアス」 IS A FACT, NOT A NUMBER (the unnumbered-extra convention). Inoue's Slam Dunk one-shot 『ピアス』 — 週刊少年ジャンプ 1998年9号, 39 pages (4 in colour), reprinted 週刊ヤングジャンプ 2001年49号, never collected in a tankōbon until THE FIRST SLAM DUNK re:SOURCE (Shueisha, 2022-12-15) — is described by both ja-WP and Oricon as 「宮城リョータの映画の物語の部分的下敷きになった作品」, i.e. PARTLY the underlying basis of the film's Ryota story. It carries no mainline chapter number (the instrument is 1-276), it is only a partial basis, and it does not make the flashback thread source content; record it as a side story of the source with its place named (a 1998 one-shot, after the serialization ended), if the ledger ever wants it.

RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY AT THE START (nothing hangs on it — a related work mints no anchors). MangaUpdates pins 223 and the film's first game beat is 223's ambush, but the tip-off itself may sit on the closing pages of ch 222 「最大の挑戦」, and I could not verify whether any pre-game beat from 216-222 (the scouting video, Anzai's word to each starter) survives in the film; no source claims one. If a page-level check is ever wanted, the film's Blu-ray chapter stops plus the vol 25 pages are the instrument.

SLIVER WATCH IN THE FLASHBACKS. ja-WP's synopsis ends the flashback thread with Mitsui petitioning to rejoin the club at the same moment Ryota returns — the manga's ch 71 beat, already adapted by the TV run's Mitsui arc. If the film restages it (from Ryota's angle), it is a sliver of already-animated material: no weight, no anchor, no change to the standing, which the game share already decides. No source states it in page terms, so it is not carried in chapters_adapted.
